macro_events.causal_chain: PPI measures wholesale inflation → leads CPI by 1-2 months → shapes Fed rate decision calculus. Cool print → yields decline → growth/tech rally → rate-cut expectations increase. Hot print → yields spike → growth-to-value rotation → dollar strengthens.
macro_events.analog: June 2024: cool CPI print triggered 4% Nasdaq rally in one week as rate-cut hopes surged
macro_events.counterargument: Single month's PPI may not shift Fed stance if underlying trends remain mixed; shelter component is the real driver of sticky CPI

macro_events.event: Iran Diplomacy / Strait of Hormuz Reopening
macro_events.causal_chain: US-Iran deal negotiations advancing → Strait of Hormuz reopening → Persian Gulf supply recovery at ~90% of pre-war volumes → oil surplus emerging (~1.2M bbl/day August) → Brent heading toward $60s → energy sector pressured → airlines/transports benefit from lower fuel → disinflationary impulse supports rate cuts.
macro_events.analog: Sep 2019 post-Abqaiq: oil spiked 15% then mean-reverted within 2 weeks as supply proved resilient
macro_events.counterargument: Any breakdown in diplomatic talks could re-spike oil immediately; surplus estimate assumes continued OPEC+ compliance

macro_events.counterargument: Overinvestment risk if AI spend plateaus; customer inventory builds could cause a 2022-style correction; geopolitical supply chain fragmentation adds cost

macro_events.event: US-China Trade Talks Resuming Late August
macro_events.causal_chain: Reciprocal tariff paused at 10% for 90 days through August → avg US tariff on Chinese goods ~33% → positive resolution could lower to 15-20% → Chinese tech (JD, NTES, BABA) and US exporters benefit → EV tariffs at 145% unlikely to change near-term → binary outcome risk for trade-sensitive names.
macro_events.analog: Jan 2020 Phase 1 deal: S&P rallied 3% in the week following announcement
macro_events.counterargument: Talks could collapse; fentanyl tariff (20%) has domestic political support and likely stays; sector-specific tariffs (EVs, solar) are structural
